question: US duties on taxed imports averaged about 59% in 1932. Besides the 1930 Smoot–Hawley Act, what pushed that rate up?
options: Falling prices, as many duties were fixed
answer: Falling prices. Many duties were set in cents per pound or per item; as import prices collapsed, the same cents became a bigger share of the price. Douglas Irwin estimates deflation explains a large part of the rise. A duty of 5 cents on a 20-cent item is 25%; at 10 cents it is 50%.
move: Before crediting a law, ask what would have happened without it.
trap: Crediting the whole rise to the famous act, since it made headlines.
reference: Irwin, Peddling Protectionism: Smoot-Hawley and the Great Depression, Princeton University Press, 2011
